# The RT64 shaders the web page builds: one shader description a line, other mode L and H, color combiner L and H,
# flags, in hex. RT64 specializes each one's WGSL when the page is built and builds them with the game waiting: those
# above the first "section" line before the game starts, and an area's section when the area first draws with its
# shaders, so that nothing draws with the ubershader, which integrated graphics can't afford (N64Recomp-browser's
# docs/porting.md, Prebuilt shader lists).
#
# Recorded by code, not by playing: node lib/N64Recomp-browser/tools/record_shaders.mjs tools/shader_plan.json build/web
# roms/dinoplanet.z64 src/rt64_shaders.txt (its header says how), on tools/build_web.sh's page. Section 0 is the
# launcher, the logos and the title, the game select and a new game's name entry as a player goes through them (A,
# and taps of the stick a game frame long on the game's clock, since the name screen moves a letter a frame). Then a
# section an area: the opening (the story point new-game) and each area the warp table reaches (docs/story-points.md),
# each started by tools/survey.js's go() from a story point and walked about for 15 s, with the object groups
# docs/story-points.md names turned on (a story point leaves them off): SwapStone Hollow's, Moon Mountain Pass's, the
# Swap Store's, and Cape Claw's at the sand worm's fight. Not recorded: the areas past their starts, the other
# areas' groups, the shrines' tests, the other bosses' fights and the game's other cutscenes.
# Flags follow settings (filtering, HDR, MSAA, upscaling), so a change to one of those defaults means recording again.
